Split the introduction by modality (#515)

* Split the introduction by modality

Move the scRNA-seq and raw data processing chapters into a new "Data basics" group under RNA.
Split the SpatialData and Squidpy half of the advanced data structures chapter into spatial/data_structures, placed after the spatial introduction, and retitle the remainder "Multimodal data structures".
Move Interoperability and GPU-accelerated analysis into a new "Interoperability and scaling" section after the modality sections, since both assume AnnData, MuData and the scanpy workflow.
AnnData/scanpy and MuData/muon stay in the introduction because every modality section builds on them.
The moved chapters keep their files in introduction/, so their URLs and the links to them from papers keep working.

Both data structure chapters were rerun on Python 3.14.7.
The MuData env pins muon 0.1.9, mudata 0.4.1 and anndata 0.12.11: muon 0.1.7 cannot import with mudata 0.4, mudata 0.3.3 cannot write with anndata 0.13, and muon's tss_enrichment still passes the dtype argument anndata 0.13 removed.
mudata 0.4 defaults display_style to "text", so the MuData summaries now render as plain text instead of the HTML widget.
spatialdata-plot 0.4 rejects table_name when coloring points by their own column, so that argument was dropped.

* Use pysam 0.24.1 wheels in the MuData chapter env

pysam 0.23.3 has no Python 3.14 wheel, so the environment build compiled it from source and failed on missing liblzma headers.
The chapter was rerun in the rebuilt environment.

* Use igraph Leiden in both data structure chapters

sc.tl.leiden without a flavor still defaults to leidenalg in scanpy 1.12, so both envs carried leidenalg only for that.
Pass flavor="igraph" and n_iterations=2 as the other chapters do, drop leidenalg from both envs, and rerun both chapters.

* Rename the closing section to "Ecosystem and performance"

* Explain the table of contents in the contributing guide

* Document pull requests, chapter execution and environment rules
